Hi Julia,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, PulseStream's Q4 traffic profile is smoothing upward and your Q2-to-Q3 token consumption shows a consistent 38% increase week-over-week on the personalization endpoints. Based on that, I've put together a short proposal to bump the monthly hosted commit and introduce a two-step tiered rate band to give you predictable unit economics during the ramp.

Proposal highlights (attached: PS_Renewal_Amendment_v2.pdf):
- Commit: increase hosted monthly commit from 400M tokens to 750M tokens (12-month term)
- Rate bands: 0-400M @ $0.0075/token, 400M-750M @ $0.0060/token (discounted mid-band)
- Burst window: +20% burst capacity for spikes, with soft-throttle threshold at 110%
- Ops: dedicated onboarding runbook and three days of throughput tuning with our infra team (redwood_throughput_plan.xlsx)
- SLA: standard Hosted SLA; we can scope a 99.9% latency SLO for the personalization route if procurement signs the amendment

Next steps I suggest:
1) You review the amendment and share any procurement/ legal feedback
2) We align on a ramp schedule (we proposed a 6-week staged rollout)
3) Ben and Marissa will coordinate the onboarding windows with your infra/ops team

Would you be able to confirm the procurement contact and any required change controls on your side? Happy to jump on a quick call next week to walk through the attachment.

Marissa — draft attached (see PS_Renewal_Amendment_v2.pdf). Core idea: bill committed usage at committed bands; any usage between 100% and 110% is treated as "soft overage" and billed at the mid-band rate. Burst up to 120% is allowed but billed as additional usage at the mid-band rate; hard throttle at >120%. We also include an ops note: continuous batching and caching configuration to be locked for first 30 days to stabilize unit economics.

I also added a clause for a single SLA exception (99.9% latency SLO) scoped to the personalization route for the term if they sign the 12-month amendment.
